name: full decomposed proof

phase_0.boundary_condition: The asymptotic limit of the extremal ratio as n approaches infinity, containing the entire decomposed proof structure within a closed topological register.

⊢.justification: The void state before any vertices or edges are instantiated, representing the initial condition where no r-cliques exist.

⊣.justification: The terminal anchor representing the closed boundary of the system where the ratio converges to a real number L.

≻.justification: The forward morphism driving the construction of larger hypergraphs by adding vertices and r-cliques toward the extremal bound.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism descending from the full hypergraph to identify forbidden k-cliques and reduce the structure to valid configurations.

⋈.justification: The composition of logical steps linking the existence of the hypergraph to the non-existence of the forbidden k-clique.

⊙.justification: The self-referential state where the system resides at the percolation threshold, recognizing its own scale-free correlations.

∈.justification: The split into two divergent paths: one maximizing clique density (T-arm) and one enforcing the forbidden k-clique constraint (F-arm).

∋.justification: The reconstitution of the two arms into a single verdict representing the limit of the ratio, fusing the constructive and refutative bounds.

⊤.justification: The affirmative state where a hypergraph exists with maximum cardinality m satisfying the r-clique condition.

⊥.justification: The negative state where the existence of a k-clique is refuted, ensuring the hypergraph remains valid.

⊞.justification: The paradice state holding both the maximal density and the forbidden constraint simultaneously at the critical threshold.

◻.justification: The permanent fixation of the limit L as a real number, an irreversible record of the asymptotic behavior.

phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: No vertices or edges exist; the hypergraph is empty and no constraints are active.
phase_3.true_description: A valid hypergraph exists with maximum r-clique density and no forbidden k-cliques.
phase_3.false_description: The hypergraph contains a forbidden k-clique or fails to meet the density requirements.
phase_3.both_description: The system is at the critical threshold where maximal density and forbidden constraints coexist in a stable paradox.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the empty hypergraph state with no vertices or edges.
Begin the forward expansion of vertices to form potential r-cliques.
Bifurcate the construction into a density maximization path and a constraint verification path.
Affirm the existence of a maximal set of r-cliques in the T-arm.
Chain the logical steps that define the cardinality m of the hypergraph.
Continue expanding the hypergraph toward the extremal bound.
Refute the existence of any k-clique in the F-arm.
Descend from the full structure to isolate and verify the forbidden subgraph condition.
Compose the verification steps ensuring no k-clique exists within any subset.
Hold the critical state where density maximization and constraint satisfaction coexist.
Recognize the system's position at the scale-free critical threshold.
Rejoin the density and constraint arms to compute the ratio of m to binomial(n,r).
Link the ratio computation to the asymptotic limit as n approaches infinity.
Permanently record the limit L as a real number.
Anchor the system at the closed boundary of the asymptotic limit.
Self-reference the completed proof structure as a closed loop.
Reset the register for the next iteration of the proof decomposition.
Re-initiate the forward morphism for a new hypergraph instance.
Split again into density and constraint paths for the new instance.
Affirm the new maximal clique set.
Refute the new forbidden k-clique.
Fuse the new arms to update the ratio sequence.
Chain the new ratio into the sequence converging to L.
Fix the new data point in the limit record.
Re-anchor the system at the updated asymptotic limit.
